title: kv-cache: improved eviction heuristics and spillover paging to reduce fragmentation & OOMs
author: Ava Thompson
description: Motivation: We observed increased fragmentation and intermittent OOMs on high-concurrency continuous-batching workloads where long-lived KV entries and variable sequence lengths cause the in-memory slab allocator to fragment and trigger expensive global evictions. This PR introduces a set of improvements to KV cache memory management and eviction policies to reduce fragmentation, enable spillover paging to host memory, and give the scheduler better signals to avoid cascading evictions. Key changes: 1) Eviction scoring: a new multi-factor eviction score that combines last-access recency, token-span contribution, per-entry fragmentation penalty, and estimated reconstruction cost. The score is tunable via config flags and exposes per-model defaults. 2) Defragmentation hints: entries now expose contiguous-run metadata to the allocator which allows the background defragger to compact hot prefixes without global stop-the-world operations. 3) Paging/spillover: a background pager thread asynchronously serializes cold KV shards to a compressed host-memory spill buffer and marks entries as paged. Paged entries remain addressable with a small async page-in path; this avoids immediate eviction when memory pressure is transient. 4) Memory accounting: per-shard soft/high watermarks and a new per-worker memory budget that cooperates with the scheduler to throttle continuous batching when paging rates exceed thresholds. 5) Metrics and tracing: added kv_cache.fragmentation_ratio, kv_cache.spillover_bytes, kv_cache.paged_entries_total and richer tracing spans around page-in/page-out to diagnose latency impact. 6) Rollout & flags: changes are gated behind a feature flag kv_cache_eviction_v2 and runtime knobs for defrag aggressiveness and spillover thresholds. Compatibility: Default behavior preserves existing semantics until the feature flag is enabled for a pool. Implementation notes: We keep the hot path allocation fast by avoiding locks in the common path and by using atomic allocation cursors with a lock-free free-list for reclaimed ranges. The pager uses bounded worker pools and backpressure to storage to avoid saturating IO when customers run on small hosts. Tests & benchmarks: Added unit tests for scoring and pager state machine, integration tests that simulate heavy continuous-batching with mixed sequence lengths, and a benchmark harness that measures end-to-end P99 generation latency under different defrag and spillover settings. Observed results: internal benchmark shows 30-45% reduction in fragmentation_ratio on long-running workloads, 40% fewer global evictions, and P99 generation latency regressions within 5% when page-in happens (median impact <1%). Deployment plan: start with a canary on Dedicated pools with conservative defaults (high spill threshold, low defrag aggressiveness), monitor metrics and tracing, then progressively enable on remaining clusters. If memory pressure increases or page-ins start affecting latency, we will rollback the feature flag and revert scheduler throttles that were introduced. See release notes and ops/upgrade notes for operator steps.

review_conversation: Ravi Patel: Can you explain how the eviction score weights are chosen? Suggest exposing them as per-pool configs rather than constants.
Ava Thompson: We added per-pool tunables and Linear task ENG-4210 to track adaptive default heuristics. The defaults are from offline traces and were validated in the benchmark harness.
Lena Müller: Concerned about page-in latency affecting P99. Are there safeguards to avoid synchronous page-ins on request path?

Ava Thompson: Page-in is async. We added a fast-path probe that returns a small opaque handle immediately and schedules page-in; the request will either proceed with a reconstruction fallback or wait on an optimized page-in future. We also added scheduler throttles and a per-worker page-in budget to bound concurrent page-ins.
Noah Kim: Tests look good. One nit: add a stress test with very small hosts (like 8GB) in CI to catch regressions.
Ava Thompson: Added a small-host stress benchmark in the benchmarks/ directory and updated CI matrix to run it on a periodic job.
Ravi Patel: LGTM after address comments.
release_notes: Improved KV cache memory management and eviction policy: new eviction scoring that reduces fragmentation, background defragmentation hints, host-memory spillover pager with async page-in, per-shard memory watermarks and scheduler cooperation. Reduces global evictions and OOMs on long-running continuous-batching workloads. Feature gated behind kv_cache_eviction_v2. Operators should follow ops/upgrade_notes/kv-cache-2026-02.md for canary rollout.
performance_impact: Benchmarks show 30-45% reduction in measured fragmentation_ratio on long-running workloads and ~40% fewer global evictions. P99 latency impact when page-in occurs is within 5% in our canary tests and median impact <1%.
tests: stress: continuous-batching with mixed sequence lengths
bench: fragmentation reduction and P99 measurement
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: page-in latency could affect tail latency under heavy memory pressure. Mitigation: feature flag rollout, conservative default thresholds, per-worker page-in budgets, scheduler throttles that reduce batch concurrency, and observability dashboards for quick rollback.
notes: Related PRs: pr-38962-kv-cache-eviction-spillover-defrag-heuristics.json and prior defrag work. Operators: update runtime config to enable kv_cache_eviction_v2 and tune thresholds for your workload.
